lesson.title: Function Notation
intro: Function notation describes how each input is assigned exactly one output.
The notation f(x) means the output of the function when x is substituted into the rule.
To evaluate a function, replace the variable with the given value and simplify carefully.
Sometimes you are given an output and must work backward to solve for the input value.

questions.prompt: Given the function g(x) = \(\frac{2x+3}{x^2-2}\), what is the value of g(-2)?
If f(x) = \(\frac{-3x-5}{2}\), what is the value of x when f(x) = -22?
questions.explanation: Solve \frac{-3x-5}{2} = -22. Multiply by 2 to get -3x - 5 = -44, then add 5 and divide by -3 to get x = 13.

questions.prompt: Given g(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x, what is the value of g(-3)?
If f(x) = \(\frac{30x^2}{x+2}\), determine the value of f\(\frac{1}{2}\).
